title: 3D Rendering in Dubai for Property and Brands | 22 Signals
description: 3D rendering for Dubai developers, interior designers and brands: photoreal exteriors, interiors, amenities, products and packaging for off-plan sales and ads.
h1: 3D rendering for Dubai developers, designers and brands
intro: We produce photoreal 3D renders and visualisation for Dubai companies: exteriors, interiors and amenities for off-plan property, fit-out concepts for interior designers, and product and packaging visuals for retail brands. You get images and 3D models ready for brochures, property portals, sales gallery screens, websites and ads, delivered on dates agreed in writing.

sections.h: Selling what has not been built yet
p: Off-plan sales are a large part of the Dubai property market, which means developers routinely sell homes that exist only as drawings. Buyers, many of them overseas, decide from a handful of images and a short film. If the renders look flat, generic or obviously computer-made, the project looks riskier than it is.

The same pressure shows up elsewhere. Interior designers pitch fit-outs for villas in Emirates Hills or offices in Business Bay before a single wall moves. Brands launching in the Gulf need product visuals before the first shipment clears Jebel Ali. Good 3D rendering, Dubai developers and designers tell us, is the difference between a confident buyer and a hesitant one.

list: Exterior architectural visualisation: towers, villas, townhouse clusters and master plans, by day, at dusk and at night.
Interior visualisation: apartments, show units, lobbies, offices, retail and hospitality spaces.
Amenity renders: pools, gyms, rooftop decks, kids' play areas and garden podiums.
Photoreal product renders for e-commerce, catalogues and campaigns.
Packaging visuals for launches, retailer presentations and marketplace listings.
Campaign visuals that combine products, people and settings without a location shoot.
3D models prepared for web viewers, configurators and ads.

sections.h: Accuracy and the rules on property imagery
p: Renders sell homes, so they need to be honest. We work from your architectural drawings, material schedules and outdoor plans, match views to what the building will actually see where you can supply the site context, and keep furniture and finishes in line with the specification buyers will receive.

Property marketing in Dubai is regulated: Dubai Land Department rules require an advertising permit for property promotions, and developers usually mark renders as artist's impressions. We leave space for permit details and disclaimers in layouts, and we flag anything in a brief that could mislead a buyer. Approving the final marketing remains with the licensed developer or broker.

list: Talk: the project, the audience, where the images will be used and the launch date.
Plan: a shot list with camera angles, times of day, mood references and delivery dates, agreed in writing.
Build: a 3D model from your drawings or CAD files, then draft renders with clay or low-detail previews for early sign-off, then final lighting and materials.
Grow: extra angles, animated walk-throughs, seasonal variants and cut-downs for social and ads.

p: We have worked with more than 30 companies across several time zones, and our 3D work is produced by the same team that makes our animation and campaign creative. For a Dubai launch that means the renders, the launch film and the ads are made together, so the building looks the same everywhere buyers see it.

We serve Dubai businesses from London, on-site when the project needs it. Rendering is naturally remote: you send drawings, references and material samples or photos, and we share previews in a review tool where you can mark up specific spots. Gulf Standard Time is four hours ahead of London in winter and three in summer, so a mark-up sent before lunch in Dubai is usually being worked on the same afternoon in London.
If a site visit would improve accuracy, for example to capture the real views from a plot or the light in a showroom, we plan it into the scope.

sections.h: Why choose 22 Signals for 3D rendering in Dubai
p: Most studios offering 3D rendering, Dubai or elsewhere, hand over a folder of images. We can also turn those images into the launch film, the project website, the portal listings and the paid campaign, under one accountable lead. Fewer suppliers means fewer mismatched visuals, fewer briefing meetings and a launch that holds its date, because one person answers for every image, film and ad that carries your project's name. Related services include animation, web development and paid media.

faqs.q: What files do you need to start a 3D rendering project?
faqs.a: Architectural drawings or CAD files, elevations, a material and finishes schedule, planting and outdoor plans if exteriors are involved, and any mood references. For products, we need dimensions, packaging artwork and photos of samples. If drawings are incomplete, we can model from sketches, though that adds time and review rounds.

faqs.q: How long does 3D rendering take for a Dubai property launch?
faqs.a: Timing for a set of exterior and interior views depends on model complexity and how quickly feedback comes back. Full launch packages with amenities and animation take longer. We work back from your launch date and agree each milestone in writing.

faqs.q: Do you render for interior designers as well as developers?
faqs.a: Yes. Interior designers and fit-out firms in Dubai use our renders to present concepts, compare material options and win client approval before work starts. We can produce several finish options from one model, which makes it easier for clients to choose and keeps revision costs down.

faqs.q: Which 3D rendering Dubai projects suit you best?
faqs.a: Projects where the renders feed a wider launch: an off-plan phase that also needs a film, a website and ads, or a product range that needs packaging visuals, e-commerce images and social content. We also take standalone image sets, but the biggest gains come when one team keeps every visual consistent.

faqs.q: Can you also make a walk-through video?
faqs.a: Yes. Once the 3D model exists, we can produce animated walk-throughs and fly-overs, amenity films and short social cuts from it. Planning the stills and the animation together saves time, because the same lighting, materials and camera work carry across both.

faqs.q: Do you need to visit the site in Dubai?
faqs.a: Usually not. Drawings, site photos and drone footage you supply are enough for most projects, and reviews happen online in hours that overlap Gulf Standard Time. When capturing the real views or light conditions would genuinely improve the result, we plan a visit and include it in the scope.

faqs.q: Are renders used in property ads regulated in Dubai?
faqs.a: Property advertising in Dubai needs a Dubai Land Department advertising permit, and renders are normally marked as artist's impressions. We leave room for permit details and disclaimers in our layouts. The developer or broker is responsible for the permit and for approving final marketing material.
